title: Bytes and endianness
body: A Java int is 32 bits. Big-endian stores the most significant byte first; little-endian stores it last. In Java 25, a newly created ByteBuffer always uses BIG_ENDIAN, and order(ByteOrder) changes it. The choice matters when another language or a socket reads the same bytes.
